title: 🌐 Enable Swahili docs translations
body:
Hello everyone!

Thank you for your interest in making FastAPI docs more accessible! 🙏

This PR enables Swahili docs translations. And it needs reviews from native speakers.

Several clarifications to make sure we are all on the same page:

* We use AI-automated workflow to update translations
* We pass 2 prompts to LLM: [general prompt](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/scripts/general-llm-prompt.md?plain=1) (not necessary to read this, just FYI) and [language-specific prompt](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/enable-Swahili/docs/sw/llm-prompt.md?plain=1). You can take a look at the examples of language-specific prompts for other languages ([es](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/docs/es/llm-prompt.md?plain=1), [ru](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/docs/ru/llm-prompt.md?plain=1), [pt](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/docs/pt/llm-prompt.md?plain=1), [de](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/docs/de/llm-prompt.md?plain=1) ...).
* As you can see, language-specific prompt contains some common terms with their translations - this is done in order to specify preferred translations for terms that have multiple alternative translations or don't have good translation (for clarity and consistency across pages). There is no goal to add as many terms as possible - we should only add terms that are needed to fix real problems in translations (when LLM translated page, but we don't like the particular translation of the term)
* We are not aiming to make translations perfect - if the meaning is clear and correct, than let's not nitpick 🤓. LLMs don't always give deterministic results, so our manual corrections might be overwritten on the next translation sync..

Our first task is to review:
* 7 pages translated in this PR ([see](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16621#issuecomment-6427868054))
* Current [language-specific prompt](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16621/changes#diff-4c05d01e08f7a0bc2f7de6c3b6a2881c6900afa3e3d6c02b951b34cc466db1ab) (I generated it with the help of Codex (GPT-6 Astra))
* Translations of the texts for docs UI (file [sw.html](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16621/changes#diff-3743892443762d92d9d7452919287bf2d05246dc90595ec3cf413da41eccafaa))


If you notice some common terms or phrases that are translated wrongly or sound awkward - please leave review comments. If others agree - I will ask you to add instructions to language-specific prompt and then I will re-translate page to see how it affects the result.

To review translated pages, you can go to [this comment](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16621#issuecomment-6427868054) and open the translated version of the page (links like `https://01249fe9.fastapitiangolo.pages.dev/sw/`) and its original English version (`English` link in the end of the same line) side by side.

When we finish with this PR I will open new PR to translate a few more pages, and we will continue reviewing them and improving the language-specific prompt.

body:
Hello @YuriiMotov! 👋 Thank you for driving the Swahili translation workflow for FastAPI. As a native Swahili speaker and active developer in the East African tech ecosystem (Kenya/Tanzania), I went through the 7 preview pages on `https://b0929535.fastapitiangolo.pages.dev/sw/` side-by-side with the English source. The translation logic and technical flow are largely intact, but the initial LLM output has a common issue we call **"over-translation" (deep translation)**: translating standard industry computing terms into literal Swahili neologisms that real software engineers never use. Here are the key observations, terms, and the comprehensive prompt rules to update `docs/sw/llm-prompt.md`: --- ### 1. Concrete Awkward Terms Observed in the 7 Preview Pages | English Term | Current AI Translation (Awkward / Misleading) | Recommended Developer Swahili | Why? | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Dependency Injection** | *Kuingiza Utegemezi* / *Utegemezi* | **Dependency Injection** | *Kuingiza utegemezi* sounds like medical injection or emotional dependency. East African developers always say "Dependency Injection". | | **Cookies / Cookie Sessions** | *Biskuti* / *Vidakuzi* | **Cookies** | *Vidakuzi* literally means edible baked cookies/biscuits. In web APIs, we always say "cookies". | | **Request Body** | *Kiini cha ombi* / *Mwili wa ombi* | **Request body** | In HTTP context, *mwili wa ombi* sounds literal and confusing. | | **Path / Query Parameters** | *Vigezo vya njia* / *Vigezo vya hoja* | **Path parameters** / **Query parameters** | Developers discuss route parameters in English. | | **Virtual Environment** | *Mazingira pepe* | **Virtual environment** | *Mazingira pepe* is academic Swahili; developers across Kenya and Tanzania universally use *virtual environment* / *venv*. | | **Headers** | *Vichwa vya habari* / *Vichwa* | **Headers** | *Vichwa vya habari* means newspaper headlines, and *vichwa* means human heads. | | **Scopes** (OAuth2) | *Upeo* | **Scopes** | *Upeo* is too abstract for OAuth2 security permissions. | --- ### 2. Syntax Fix: MkDocs Heading Anchors On the home page (`index.md`), the sponsors headers had broken anchor formatting: * Current: `## Sponsors #sponsors` * Fix needed: `## Sponsors { #sponsors }` (FastAPI's MkDocs theme requires `{ #anchor }` syntax, otherwise the anchor text renders as literal text). --- ### 3. Proposed Full `docs/sw/llm-prompt.md` We crafted a comprehensive prompt with explicit **negative constraints** (banning literal translations of 40+ computing terms) and natural grammatical rules (e.g. Swahili prefix verbs like *ku-validate*, *ku-serialize*). You can view the full file on GitHub: 👉 **[official_fastapi_swahili_pages/llm-prompt.md](https://github.com/Eminek-marz/fastapi-swahili-localization/blob/main/official_fastapi_swahili_pages/llm-prompt.md)**
Click here to view / copy the full proposed docs/sw/llm-prompt.md ```markdown # Mwongozo wa Kutafsiri Nyaraka za FastAPI kwa Kiswahili (Swahili Localization Prompt) Wewe ni mtaalamu wa kutafsiri nyaraka za kiufundi za programu (software documentation) kutoka Kiingereza kwenda lugha ya Kiswahili fasaha kinachotumiwa na wasanidi programu (developers) kote Afrika Mashariki (Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, DRC). Lengo lako kuu ni kutoa tafsiri ya asili, inayosomeka vizuri, inayoeleweka haraka, na **isiyo na tafsiri nzito au ya kulazimisha (avoid deep translation / literal over-translation)**. --- ## Kanuni Kuu (Golden Rules) ### 1. Falsafa ya "Bila Deep Translation" (Developer Loan Words) Wasanidi programu wa Kiswahili hutumia maneno mengi ya kiufundi ya Kiingereza katika mazungumzo na kazi zao za kila siku. **USITAFSIRI** maneno ya kiufundi ya programu kuwa Kiswahili cha kizamani au maneno yasiyoeleweka. * **Tumia maneno asilia ya Kiingereza kwa istilahi za kodi na usanifu.** * Mfano: Tumia **Dependency Injection** (KAMWE usiseme "Kuingiza Utegemezi" au "Udungaji wa Vitegemezi"). * Mfano: Tumia **virtual environment** (KAMWE usiseme "mazingira pepe"). * Mfano: Tumia **cookies** (KAMWE usiseme "biskuti" au "vidakuzi"). * Mfano: Tumia **request body** (KAMWE usiseme "kiini cha ombi" au "mwili wa ombi"). * Mfano: Tumia **headers** (KAMWE usiseme "vichwa vya habari" au "vichwa"). * Mfano: Tumia **path parameters** (KAMWE usiseme "vigezo vya njia"). ### 2. Uundaji wa Vitenzi vya Kiteknolojia (Verbs with English Roots) Katika Kiswahili cha kiteknolojia, vitendo vya kikompyuta huundwa kwa kuongeza kiambishi kiambata cha Kiswahili `ku-` au viambishi ngeli kwenye neno la Kiingereza badala ya kutunga neno jipya lisilojulikana: * **Validate** -> *ku-validate* au *kuhakiki* * **Serialize / Deserialize** -> *ku-serialize* / *ku-deserialize* * **Deploy** -> *ku-deploy* * **Parse** -> *ku-parse* * **Mount** -> *ku-mount* * **Inject** -> *ku-inject* ### 3. Matumizi ya Ngeli Sahihi za Kiswahili Majina mengi ya kiteknolojia ya Kiingereza huwekwa katika **Ngeli ya I-ZI (Ngeli ya 9/10)**: * *Framework hii ni ya kisasa* (si "framework huyu") * *Response hii inachujwa* (si "response huyu") * *Model hii inatumika* (si "model huyu") * *Dependency hii inafanya kazi* ### 4. Uhifadhi wa Syntax za MkDocs na Markdown (CRITICAL) FastAPI hutumia mfumo wa MkDocs Material wenye sheria kali za muundo: * **Headers zenye Anchors**: Usibadilishe muundo wa `{ #anchor-name }`. * Sahihi: `## Sponsors { #sponsors }` * Sio: `## Sponsors #sponsors` * **Vizuizi Maalum vya Admonitions**: * Hifadhi `/// note`, `/// tip`, `/// warning`, `/// danger`, `/// details` bila kubadilisha alama za mshazari `///`. * Unaweza kutafsiri kichwa pekee: `/// note | Kumbuka` au `/// tip | Kidokezo`. * **Kodi na Snippets**: Kamwe usitafsiri kodi ya Python, majina ya variable, majina ya function, au nukuu za `{* ... *}`. --- ## Jedwali la Msamiati Maalum (Technical Vocabulary Mapping) | Istilahi ya Kiingereza (English) | Tafsiri Inayotakiwa (Preferred Swahili) | TAFSIRI ILIYOPIGWA MARUKUKU (FORBIDDEN) | Sababu / Maelezo | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Dependency Injection** | **Dependency Injection** | *Kuingiza utegemezi*, *udungaji* | "Udungaji" linamaanisha sindano ya hospitali. Wasanidi programu hutumia jina asilia la kiingereza. | | **Dependency / Dependencies** | **Dependency / Dependencies** au *vitegemezi* | *Mitegemeo* | Kwenye kodi na mifumo, baki na "dependencies". Kwenye sentensi za kawaida unaweza kutumia "vitegemezi". | | **Cookies / Cookie Sessions** | **Cookies** | *Biskuti*, *vidakuzi* | "Vidakuzi/biskuti" ni vyakula. Katika wavuti na HTTP, tumia "cookies". | | **Headers** | **Headers** | *Vichwa*, *vichwa vya habari* | "Vichwa" ni vya binadamu, "vichwa vya habari" ni vya magazeti. Katika mitandao ni "headers". | | **Request Body** | **Request body** | *Mwili wa ombi*, *kiini cha ombi* | Baki na "request body" ili msomaji aelewe inarejelea HTTP body. | | **Path Parameter** | **Path parameter** | *Kigezo cha njia* | "Kigezo cha njia" kinachanganya sana. | | **Query Parameter** | **Query parameter** | *Kigezo cha hoja* | "Hoja" inamaanisha argument au dispute. Baki na "query parameter". | | **Virtual Environment** | **Virtual environment** au *venv* | *Mazingira pepe* | "Mazingira pepe" ni lugha ya kitaaluma isiyotumiwa na watengenezaji programu vitendoni. | | **Field / Fields** | **Field / Fields** | *Uwanja / nyanja* | "Uwanja" ni wa mpira. Katika Pydantic models na fomu ni "field". | | **Endpoint / Path operation** | **Endpoint / Path operation** | *Kituo cha mwisho* | "Kituo cha mwisho" ni kituo cha basi/gari moshi. | | **Concurrency** | **Concurrency** | *Uwandani*, *sambamba* | Eleza kwa mifano lakini istilahi yenyewe ibaki "concurrency". | | **Parallelism** | **Parallelism** | *Usambamba* | Inaweza kutumika kama "parallelism" au kueleza kama kufanya kazi sambamba. | | **Rollback** | **Rollback** | *Kubiringika nyuma*, *kurejesha nyuma* | Katika database transactions, baki na "kufanya rollback". | | **Scopes** | **Scopes** | *Upeo* | "Upeo" hauelezi ruhusa za kiusalama za OAuth2. Tumia "scopes". | | **Payload** | **Payload** | *Mzigo* | "Mzigo" unaleta picha ya usafirishaji wa mizigo ya bandarini. | | **Middleware** | **Middleware** | *Programu ya kati* | Istilahi ya kiufundi ibaki "middleware". | | **CORS** | **CORS** | *Kugawana rasilimali asilia* | Kifupi cha kimataifa cha kiufundi hakitafsiriwi. |

title: docs: add blocking and long-running work section to WebSockets
body:
## Description

The WebSockets page doesn't mention that WebSocket handlers are always `async def`: unlike *path operation functions*, there's no plain `def` option where FastAPI runs the function in an external threadpool. Because of this, users coming from HTTP endpoints naturally assume the same `def`-threadpool escape hatch exists, run blocking code in a WebSocket handler, and freeze every other connection in the app.

This is a recurring confusion point (see the discussions on running long CPU-bound tasks without dropping WebSocket connections) and it is currently covered nowhere: `async.md` explains the threadpool mechanism for `def` *path operation functions* but never mentions WebSockets, and `advanced/websockets.md` never mentions blocking code or the event loop.

Adds a short section to the WebSockets page stating:

- WebSocket handlers are always `async def`; no `def`-threadpool option exists.
- Blocking or CPU-bound code in a handler stops the event loop and freezes every other connection.
- For blocking I/O, use `await run_in_threadpool(...)` from `fastapi.concurrency` (verified: it is exported there, and FastAPI's routing asserts WebSocket endpoints must be async).
- A tip that a threadpool doesn't help long CPU-bound work, which belongs in a separate process with progress sent back over the socket.

## Docs preview

Open the Netlify preview for this PR to read the new section in context.

@YuriiMotov, Oooh I get it now.
With direct translation, we are losing the initial meaning of the documentation e.g.:

 Udungaji wa vitegemezi: the intended meaning is Dependency Injection, but the resultant meaning in Swahili is "vaccination of those who depend".
 Parameters ("kigezo"): the Swahili word used here means point of reference or criteria.
 Headers ("vichwa"): it loosely translates to human heads, so keeping the word in English is a better option.
 Cookies ("vidakuzi"): it literally sounds like "Little gossipers" (from udaku).
 Background task ("kazi ya chinichini"): in Swahili this means sneaky/underhanded dealings.
 Class ("darasa"): this means a school classroom.

We should use English loan words for technical terms to preserve the meaning and prevent the documentation from losing its intended message.

title: docs: note that blocking work in WebSocket handlers stalls the event loop
body:
Supersedes #16628, which was closed with a suggestion to gather feedback in a discussion first.

**Discussion:** https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16629

@vladduucckk confirmed the asymmetry is worth documenting:

> FastAPI automatically runs regular def HTTP endpoints in a threadpool, so you can use blocking code there without thinking much about it. But with WebSockets it works differently, and I think thats something worth mentioning in the docs.

and asked for a smaller footprint than my original section, plus a caveat I had underplayed:

> I wouldnt add a whole section for this though. Just a small note explaining the difference and maybe a link to async.md would be enough. Also worth mentioning that run_in_threadpool is fine for blocking I/O, but it wont magically solve CPU-heavy operations.

## What this adds

The WebSockets page currently never mentions the event loop. `async.md` explains the threadpool for `def` *path operation functions* but never mentions WebSockets, so users reasonably assume the same escape hatch exists there.

The note now sits at roughly half the original length: one paragraph on the `def`-threadpool asymmetry and what it means for other connections, one line on `await run_in_threadpool(...)`, and a tip that CPU-bound work belongs in a separate process. The [Async and Await](../async.md#async-and-await) reference is kept and scoped to the sentence explaining the threadpool mechanism, rather than restating it.

No code changes; docs only. Happy to cut it further, fold it into a tip on the existing page, or drop it entirely if the maintainers judge it too basic for the page.

title: ⚡️ Match nested included routers in a single pass
body:
Fixes the slowdown with nested routers reported in #16620.

Since 0.137, routing a request walks the router tree several times: `_get_routes_version()` walks the whole subtree on every call, and each level matches its subtree again in `handle()`.

* A router change now also bumps the version of the routers that include it, so checking the version doesn't walk the tree.
* Each included router caches the flat list of routes in its subtree and matches it once per request. `matches()` passes the matched route to `handle()` in the child scope.
* Routers that override `matches()` or `handle()`, and routes that override `matches()`, are still called as before.

Benchmark from #16620 (300 routes: 20 groups × 15 routers, same machine), µs per request:

| | first route | last route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.136.3 | 62 | 285 |
| master | 303 | 2134 |
| this PR | 79 | 118 |
